title: Get explained writing suggestions in Google Docs from AI
summary: A developer built an open-source Google Docs add-on where Gemini reviews text, tables and charts and leaves tracked suggestions with reasons to accept or reject.
agent_role: The add-on pulls tables and figures from the document and sends them to Gemini. It inserts suggested edits with a reason and a learning point, and comments on tables and charts. The writer decides which suggestions to accept or reject. The author says Gemini 4 Argon also helped build the app.
what_they_did: Tanaike built DocuMentor AI, a Google Docs add-on, with help from Gemini 4 Argon. It reads a whole document tab or a selection, including tables and charts. It uploads figures to Gemini for a short time, then deletes them. It places edits as Docs suggestions rather than rewriting your text. Each suggestion gets a comment explaining why and what to learn, plus an end summary from a 'writing coach'.
worth_knowing: The point is to keep you thinking. You must accept or reject every change yourself instead of pasting in AI rewrites.
prompt: Review my Google Doc [document link] as a writing coach. Read the text, tables and any charts. Do not change my text directly. Propose each edit as a suggestion, and explain in one line why you suggest it and what I can learn from it. Flag any numbers in the text that don't match the charts or tables. End with a short summary of my most common writing habits to work on.

curation.rationale: Open-source add-on where an AI reads text, tables and charts and places tracked suggestions with explanations in Google Docs. It was itself built with Gemini. Light on results, but code is available.
